summary: Read-only cross-layer audit of current MIO working tree, including unforeseen failures and cashier usability under real workloads.
approval: User explicitly requests a comprehensive audit/test approach across Java, SQL, UI and business workflows, with AGY doing source reading and Codex planning/review. No production DB writes. Include multi-persona cashier and service/appointment scenarios. Existing approved repair scope permits fixing verified defects and isolated-test DB only.

tasks.goal: Find additional high-impact defects in current project code/schema beyond already recorded A01-A15 and repair regressions; prioritize what can be verified and repaired quickly.
tasks.design: Audit current working tree, not stale baseline. Trace UI -> BUS -> DAO -> Entity -> SQL for invoice/product price provenance, barcode-first cashier flow, dashboard aggregation vs persisted data, large invoice/product/service queues, return/refund/stock/loyalty, appointment late/no-show/cancel/reschedule, employee shift/permissions, and transactional failure paths. Review SQL schema vs every referenced table/column in these paths and flag migration ordering/backfill hazards. Simulate at least four operator personas: novice cashier, high-volume scan cashier, interruption/error-prone cashier, service/appointment manager handling a long queue. For each scenario trace actual handlers and state changes; do not claim actual usability tests without UI runtime. Identify unseen edge cases as well as user-provided examples. Treat no-show statuses and unpriced-product policy as decisions still open; present policy options, avoid changing them. For each finding report source file:method and exact relevant lines/branches, reproduction trigger/steps, severity, observed-vs-inferred evidence, customer/employee impact, smallest safe fix, relevant module owner from existing plan, and whether isolated DB/UI evidence is required. Distinguish already-fixed/covered findings from new findings. No code or SQL edits, no commands, no DB operations, no Git, no secrets. Keep output concise and rank P0/P1 first; recommend a same-day repair order with dependencies and minimum regression cases.
tasks.askWhen: Return a precise blocker if required source is missing. Do not invent product-policy decisions or runtime evidence.
steps: Read AGY_HANDOVER_20261108.md, source audit baseline, current authorization and relevant Java/SQL source
Trace each persona and cross-layer data flow, identifying cases not covered by prior regressions
Return prioritized source-grounded findings, safe repair shortlist, and exact regression scenarios
acceptance: Audit describes current working-tree behavior and cites exact source locations
Findings distinguish code-proven defects, likely risks and unresolved policy choices
SQL mapping claims identify specific Java query/table/column against schema definition
Persona scenarios include cashier steps, system response, bottleneck/failure and operational impact
Fix shortlist respects existing module ownership and identifies dependencies
No edits or unsupported claims of live UI/database testing

checks.description: Codex verifies each source claim against current code/schema and keeps UI/DB runtime evidence separate.
